//: The DECLARED dependency-naming-field census read by
check-dependency-fields-honoured — the ONE gate C79 §7 and C78 §20 (U-INV-6)
SHARE. Two gates over one invariant is the second-copy disease C79 §6.5 exists
to forbid, applied to gates; this file is the single ledger.
THE INVARIANT (C79 §7.2, C78 §3.3): for every field that NAMES a dependency,
exactly one of — (a) POPULATE it on every path that writes the record, (b)
REMOVE it from the schema, (c) DECLARE it at its declaration site as
not-yet-populated with an owner and a closing condition, registered as a NAMED
GAP. 'Leaving it as an empty array is none of these three.'
THE CENSUS, AND WHY THIS LEDGER READS 15 WHERE C79 SAYS 14.
C79 §0.1(5) and §9(3) cite the Phase 0 measurement: 14 fields name a
dependency, 2 are honoured, 12 are not. Re-measured against the working tree on
2026-08-12, the SUBSTANCE is unchanged — the same fields, the same two honoured
(hostSlabId on floors, hostId on slab sketch edges), the same defects — but the
The difference is granularity in the source table, not a new defect.
BIM30-PHASE0-RELATIONSHIP-INVENTORY.md §4.1 gives `boundingWallIds` TWO rows
(FloorData, CeilingData) and `hostRoomId` TWO rows (FloorData, CeilingData),
but collapses `coveredRoomIds` into ONE row spanning `FloorData`/`CeilingData`.
The 14 is therefore a count of TABLE ROWS at inconsistent grain, not of
(field × element type) pairs. This ledger uses the consistent grain — one row
per field per declaring type — because that is the grain at which C79 §7.2's
disposition is actually CHOSEN: floors and ceilings are written by two
different commands, and either could be fixed without the other. §7.4 exists
precisely because a field can be honoured on one write path and empty on
another, so a census that cannot express that distinction cannot police it.
This is a CONTRADICTION WITH THE CONTRACT'S STATED NUMBER and is recorded
loudly rather than absorbed. C79 §0.1(5), §9(3) and §8's minimum-evidence cell
all say 14/12; the honest reading at consistent grain is 15/13. Nothing got
worse — one row was split in two. The floor below is set at the contract's 14
so the ledger can never shrink BELOW the cited census, and the gate prints both
numbers on every run so the discrepancy stays visible until C79 is amended.
DISPOSITION VOCABULARY (C79 §7.2's own three, plus the two states a field can
be in BEFORE one of them is chosen):
POPULATE  — (a). The field is written with real ids on every write path AND a
reactor re-derives when the named element changes. This is the
only disposition that makes a row HONOURED.
REMOVE    — (b). Struck from the schema. The row leaves this ledger entirely.
DECLARE   — (c). Annotated at the declaration site with owner + closing
condition. The gate CHECKS the annotation is actually there.
EMPTY     — the §7.1 anti-pattern: written with a value that cannot express a
dependency (`: []`). None of the three. A FINDING.
UNREACTED — written with real ids, but nothing reacts to the named element
changing. Also none of the three. A FINDING.
PARTIAL   — §7.3: read for a purpose OTHER than the dependency the name
promises (hostRoomId drives finish COLOUR; the boundary is never
re-derived). A partial honouring recorded as a full one. FINDING
unless the declaration site says so.
WHY THE ROWS ARE DECLARED AND NOT DISCOVERED. A regex for 'a field whose name
contains an id and names another element' has no way to tell `hostSlabId` (a
dependency) from `id` (identity) or `systemTypeId` (a catalogue lookup), and no
way at all to decide whether anything REACTS — which is the entire question.
The census was made by reading. The gate re-measures each declared row against
its own write site and reactor site, in BOTH directions, so neither a
regression nor a silent fix passes unnoticed.
declaredFindings is NAMED and SHRINK-ONLY. Each entry is '<field>@<owner>'.
A row that reaches POPULATE, REMOVE or DECLARE leaves the list in the commit
that moves it.
